column1: # Declared absences: series files a target legitimately builds no object from.
# scripts/checkseries.sh compiles every translation unit the patch series
# touches. A unit that produces no object on a target is not automatically a
# pass any more -- "this file does not apply here" and "nobody checked this
# file" were the same word until the ffmpeg codec list showed what that costs,
# so an absence has to be accounted for or the gate fails as `unexplained`.
# Two of the four accounts are derived and never appear here:
#   compiles      an object was produced from the file.
#   include-only  the file is no translation unit of its own, and an object
#                 this gate compiled recorded reading it. Verified from the
#                 compiler's own dependencies, so it is not a declaration
#                 anyone can get wrong.
# The other two are human statements about a build configuration, which no
# build graph can distinguish from an oversight, so they are written down here
# and reviewed:
#   platform      the GN condition that selects the file excludes this target.
#   config        this build's configuration excludes it, e.g. a GN arg.
# FORMAT  path <TAB> target-globs <TAB> category <TAB> evidence
#   target-globs  comma-separated fnmatch patterns over the gate target name
#                 ("windows-*", "linux-arm64"). List only the targets the
#                 absence is expected on: a declaration matching a target that
#                 does compile the file is stale and fails the gate, which is
#                 what stops this file from rotting into a blanket exemption.
#   evidence      the GN condition or patch that scopes the file. It must be
#                 something a reader can open and check.
# Checked in both directions: a missing row fails the run as unexplained, and
# a row this run disproves fails it as stale.
base/system/sys_info_posix.cc

column1: # The list files are include-only, and they are verified as such on linux-x64,
# where allcodecs.c and parsers.c read exactly these two. They cannot be
# verified anywhere else, because they are not the files anyone else reads:
# third_party/ffmpeg/BUILD.gn:14 puts chromium/config/$ffmpeg_branding/
# $os_config/$ffmpeg_arch on the include path, ffmpeg_options.gni:63 sets
# `os_config = current_os` and only overrides it for msan, ChromeOS/Fuchsia,
# and `is_win && !is_clang`, and ffmpeg_arch follows current_cpu. So each
# target reads its own config directory's copy: windows-x64 reads win/x64, not
# win-msvc/x64, because build/args/windows-x64.gn:5 sets `is_clang = true`.
# Confirmed empirically on the macos-arm64 graph, where `ninja -t deps` for
# allcodecs.o names config/Chrome/mac/arm64/libavcodec/codec_list.c.
# Each config directory's pair is therefore verifiable on exactly one target
# and declared on the other three. After patch 0109 three directories carry an
# HEVC entry -- linux/x64 (0061), linux/arm64 and win/x64 (0109). mac/arm64
# stays at zero deliberately: media/gpu/mac/video_toolbox_video_decoder.cc:521
# passes HEVCPROFILE_MIN..HEVCPROFILE_MAX on any macOS host, so the software
# decoder is not needed there.
third_party/ffmpeg/chromium/config/Chrome/linux/x64/libavcodec/codec_list.c
column4: only a Linux x64 toolchain puts chromium/config/Chrome/linux/x64 on the ffmpeg include path (third_party/ffmpeg/BUILD.gn:14 with os_config/ffmpeg_arch from ffmpeg_options.gni). NOT absent on linux-arm64: that target cross-compiles on an x64 host and builds allcodecs.c twice, so the x64 host toolchain reads this copy while the arm64 target toolchain reads linux/arm64
